answer: Every identity grows one kernel, and its payout is set by sounding it: three strangers drop a copper line into the lagoon and measure how deep the kernel's real work runs, so a shell with no depth earns nothing. Payouts settle only at low tide, when the lagoon drains and every kernel's depth lies visible at once — clones grown from one operator all show the same shallow depth, exposing the fleet as one root. Each sounding costs copper that doubles per kernel from one funding trail, so n clones pay 1+2+4... while sharing one shallow harvest, and the fleet drowns in its own sounding fees.
